assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a scalar boson at 125 GeV completed the Standard Model and was the clearest clue from nature in a generation. The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical mechanism and explicitly left the experimental discovery for later. This is the discovery-first case: unambiguous, central, and with lasting consequences for every later question about electroweak symmetry breaking and naturalness.
assessment.attribution: The collaborations involved thousands of people, but the proposers and long-standing leaders of the ATLAS and CMS projects (spokespersons and conceptual drivers of the detectors) offer a defensible three-person configuration. Credit for the 2012 analyses is diffuse and some members of the committee may prefer a different mix, such as including accelerator or analysis leadership.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature: independent confirmation by two experiments, Run 2 and Run 3 coupling and spin-parity measurements, and more than a decade of stability. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Which individuals best represent a collaboration of thousands is a judgement about credit that the supplied record cannot settle.
I rely on my own background knowledge of ATLAS and CMS leadership roles and have not verified them independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos beyond the atmospheric background, followed by evidence for a neutrino source (TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane), opened a new window on the high-energy universe. It is a discovery made from real data about the cosmos, with the 2002 prize for cosmic neutrinos as precedent for the field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the scientific driver of the IceCube concept and Spiering a long-standing leader of the collaboration and of earlier detector efforts. A two-person prize looks fair on the supplied credit, though the role of AMANDA pioneers and of the instrumentation builders could be argued.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is well established by several independent analysis channels. Source identification is still limited to a few objects and the origin of the bulk flux remains open, which tempers but does not undermine the discovery of the neutrino sky.
uncertainties: Individual source associations are still statistically modest and the origin of most neutrinos is unknown.
Division of credit between the IceCube and earlier AMANDA/Baikal efforts is not fully resolved in the supplied record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, now reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and have redefined what precision measurement can test, from relativistic redshift across millimetres to searches for variation of constants and dark-matter signals. Clear, original and of lasting impact, with a natural link to fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first demonstrated the magic-wavelength lattice scheme; Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and combined it with frequency combs and many-body effects. The two-person allocation is clean. Ye also appears in the nuclear-clock candidate, which could complicate a joint award later.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently reproduced across many laboratories, with ongoing work toward a redefinition of the second. The 2005 prize covered the frequency comb and the 2012 prize ion-trap manipulation, so the timing for lattice clocks is plausible.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the achievement as a distinct discovery or as an evolution of earlier clock prizes.
Competing claims from ion-clock and lattice-clock communities are not assessed here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicting flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by observed correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, created the moire quantum materials field and is a rare case of a prediction confirmed in the laboratory with enormous follow-on activity.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group the decisive experiments. These three names give a theory-plus-experiment configuration that is easy to defend. Other groups (for example Dean, Yacoby, Young, Efetov) also made major contributions and would be left out.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is broad and independent across many groups within eight years, but the microscopic mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated. Recognition may be slightly early, yet the discovery itself is clear.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for the superconductivity is not settled.
Relative credit for the experimental discovery among several groups is contested to some degree.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The double pulsar, the only known system with two detectable radio pulsars, has given the most stringent strong-field tests of general relativity, including multiple independent post-Keplerian relations checked at the 0.01 percent level. It is clear, quantitative evidence about gravity in the strong-field regime, which matters to anyone sceptical of unconfirmed gravitational theory.
assessment.attribution: Burgay found the first pulsar and Lyne led the discovery of the second; Kramer led the timing and tests of gravity. The three names map well onto discovery and interpretation. Hulse and Taylor already received the 1993 prize for the first binary pulsar, so a novelty argument must be made.
assessment.maturity: Stable and independently cross-checked across more than two decades of timing. The relativity tests keep improving and no deviations have been found.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the 1993 prize.
The role of other members of the Parkes team in the discovery is not captured by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first resolved images of the shadow of M87* and Sgr A* directly test the strong-field regime near a horizon and are visually and conceptually striking. As a theorist working on horizonless alternatives I regard them as important constraints, though the images themselves are model-dependent in interpretation.
assessment.attribution: The collaboration is large. Falcke proposed the imaging of the shadow, Doeleman led the global VLBI effort and Zensus built European and facility leadership. The three-name option is plausible but contentious; several other leaders would be omitted.
assessment.maturity: Imaging is established with repeated epochs and a second source, but the constraints on gravity theories and on horizonless objects are still modest, so the long-term scientific payoff is incomplete.
uncertainties: Strength of tests of general relativity from the images is limited and model dependent.
Attribution inside a collaboration of hundreds is unresolved, and my own interest in black-hole mimickers is a potential bias.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced the precision map of CMB anisotropies that fixed the cosmological parameters of the standard model at percent level and confirmed an almost flat universe with dark energy. It was a decisive set of clues from nature, building on the COBE prize of 2006 and the 2019 cosmology prize.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Spergel led the theoretical analysis and Page led instrument design and scientific analysis. A three-person allocation is workable but the contribution of the many team members, and of Planck, complicates the picture.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed by Planck, ground-based experiments and large-scale structure. The scientific milestone is well established, though its novelty has been partly absorbed by earlier cosmology prizes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 and 2019 prizes may weaken the case.
Credit relative to Planck leaders and the broader WMAP team is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Trapping and cooling antihydrogen, spectroscopy of the 1S-2S line, and comparison of proton and antiproton properties provide direct tests of CPT symmetry and of antimatter gravity. These experiments address the matter-antimatter asymmetry with null results that constrain theories, which is valuable evidence from nature.
assessment.attribution: Hangst leads the ALPHA antihydrogen programme, Gabrielse developed antiproton and positron trapping and the ATRAP effort, and Ulmer leads BASE with the most precise antiproton magnetic moment. Credit seems separable into complementary achievements, though the allocation is not trivial.
assessment.maturity: The results are repeated and improving, but they are null, so the field is still maturing and the leading precision may change. Interpretation is stable but recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: Whether null CPT results are viewed as a discovery or as a continuing precision programme.
Credit among ALPHA, ATRAP, ATHENA and BASE contributors is not fully clear.
